points.quote: An application is a package whose `dependencies` list the extensions it wants. ... `theia build`, from `@theia/cli`, does the following:
A Theia extension is an ordinary npm package, such as those under `/packages/`. Its `package.json` has a `theiaExtensions` array. Each entry names a frontend module, a backend module, or both
`src/browser`: frontend code that runs in the browser. `src/node`: backend code that runs in Node.

Each of those files is an InversifyJS `ContainerModule`. It binds services and contributions, such as `CommandContribution`, `MenuContribution`, `KeybindingContribution` and `FrontendApplicationContribution`.

`src/browser`: frontend code that runs in the browser. `src/node`: backend code that runs in Node. `src/common`: code shared by both, such as protocols and interfaces. `src/electron-browser` and `src/electron-main`: Electron renderer and main-process code.
It also has a `theia` section with `frontend.config` and `backend.config`. Those hold the application name, default preferences and similar settings.

It generates frontend and backend entry files. ... It generates an `esbuild.mjs` config, and esbuild bundles the frontend. ... `npm run start:browser` runs the generated backend. That backend is an Express server ... It serves the bundled frontend at localhost:3000. ... The Electron app follows the same pattern, with the backend run from the Electron main process.
